**Djamel Belmadi** ([Arabic](/wiki/Arabic_language "Arabic language"): جَمَال
بَلمَاضِيّ; born 25 March 1976) is a professional
[football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") coach and former
player. He is the current head coach of [Qatar Stars
League](/wiki/Qatar_Stars_League "Qatar Stars League") side [Al
Duhail](/wiki/Al_Duhail_SC "Al Duhail SC"). Born in France, he represented
Algeria internationally between 2000 and 2004.

As a player he was [midfielder](/wiki/Midfielder "Midfielder") who had spells
in [Ligue 1](/wiki/Ligue_1 "Ligue 1") with [Paris Saint-
Germain](/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_F.C. "Paris Saint-Germain F.C."),
[Marseille](/wiki/Olympique_de_Marseille "Olympique de Marseille"),
[Cannes](/wiki/AS_Cannes "AS Cannes") and [Valenciennes](/wiki/Valenciennes_FC
"Valenciennes FC"). He also briefly played in [La Liga](/wiki/La_Liga "La
Liga") for [Celta Vigo](/wiki/Celta_de_Vigo "Celta de Vigo") and in the
[Premier League](/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League") for [Manchester
City](/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C."). Later on in his
career he returned to [England](/wiki/England "England") and played several
seasons at [Southampton](/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C.") whilst the
club were in the [Football League](/wiki/Football_League "Football League").
He also played for [Martigues](/wiki/FC_Martigues "FC Martigues"), [Al-
Ittihad](/wiki/Al-Gharrafa_Sports_Club "Al-Gharrafa Sports Club") and [Al-
Kharitiyath](/wiki/Al-Kharitiyath_Sports_Club "Al-Kharitiyath Sports Club").
Born in [France](/wiki/France "France"), he played internationally for
[Algeria](/wiki/Algeria_national_football_team "Algeria national football
team") and was capped 20 times.

As a coach, Belmadi has managed [Lekhwiya](/wiki/Lekhwiya_SC "Lekhwiya SC"),
[Qatar B](/wiki/Qatar_national_football_team "Qatar national football team"),
[Qatar](/wiki/Qatar_national_football_team "Qatar national football team"),
[Al-Duhail](/wiki/Al-Duhail_SC "Al-Duhail SC")[a] and most recently, Algeria.

## Club career

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Djamel_Belmadi&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section:
Club career")]

### France and Spain

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Djamel_Belmadi&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section:
France and Spain")]

Born in [Champigny-sur-Marne](/wiki/Champigny-sur-Marne "Champigny-sur-
Marne"), France, Belmadi started his career at [Paris Saint-
Germain](/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_F.C. "Paris Saint-Germain F.C."), making
his debut in January 1996 against [Gueugnon](/wiki/FC_Gueugnon "FC Gueugnon"),
before spending a season at [Martigues](/wiki/FC_Martigues "FC Martigues"). He
spent the 1997–98 season at [Marseille](/wiki/Olympique_de_Marseille
"Olympique de Marseille"), and then moved to [Cannes](/wiki/AS_Cannes "AS
Cannes") for the 1998–99 season. In August 1999, he was signed again by
Marseille, but immediately went on loan to Spanish club [Celta
Vigo](/wiki/Celta_de_Vigo "Celta de Vigo").

In January 2000, Belmadi returned to Marseille, eventually securing a regular
place in the first team's midfield in 2000–01. In January 2001, he made good
use of a rare opportunity presented him to play in Marseille's attack, when
Liberian maestro [George Weah](/wiki/George_Weah "George Weah")—who had been
the main attacker—was away on international duty with the Lone Stars of
[Liberia](/wiki/Liberia_national_football_team "Liberia national football
team"). Belmadi seized the opportunity to score a vital goal for Marseille
against fellow strugglers [Toulouse](/wiki/Toulouse_FC "Toulouse FC") to keep
Marseille just outside the relegation zone.

On 14 April 2001, he scored the winning goal in Marseille's 2–1 victory over
[Sedan](/wiki/CS_Sedan_Ardennes "CS Sedan Ardennes"), before a near–60,000
crowd, giving [Bernard Tapie](/wiki/Bernard_Tapie "Bernard Tapie")'s team a
much needed lifeline out of relegation.

### Manchester City

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Djamel_Belmadi&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section:
Manchester City")]

In January 2003, Belmadi had fallen out of favour at Marseille, now managed by
[Alain Perrin](/wiki/Alain_Perrin "Alain Perrin"), who agreed to loan him to
[Kevin Keegan](/wiki/Kevin_Keegan "Kevin Keegan")’s [Manchester
City](/wiki/Manchester_City_F.C. "Manchester City F.C.") after a successful
trial. He joined ranks with fellow Algerian [Ali Benarbia](/wiki/Ali_Benarbia
"Ali Benarbia").

He made his full debut for Manchester City on 29 January 2003 at [Maine
Road](/wiki/Maine_Road "Maine Road") in a 4–1 victory against
[Fulham](/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C.") (alongside another recruit from the
French league – [David Sommeil](/wiki/David_Sommeil "David Sommeil")).

In Belmadi's brief time at Manchester City, he only made two starts and six
substitute appearances, the last of which was in a 1–0 defeat against
[Southampton](/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C.") on 11 May 2003 in the
final league game at Maine Road.

Although Kevin Keegan liked Belmadi's style of play, he conceded that he could
not afford another free spirit in a side already containing [Eyal
Berkovic](/wiki/Eyal_Berkovic "Eyal Berkovic") and Ali Bernabia, so Belmadi
returned to Marseille.

In August 2003, he was released by Marseille and played the 2003–04 and
2004–05 seasons in [Qatar](/wiki/Qatar "Qatar") with [Al-Ittihad](/wiki/Al-
Gharrafa_Sports_Club "Al-Gharrafa Sports Club") and [Al-Kharitiyath](/wiki/Al-
Kharitiyath_Sports_Club "Al-Kharitiyath Sports Club").

### Southampton

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Djamel_Belmadi&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section:
Southampton")]

In July 2005, after trials at [Celtic](/wiki/Celtic_F.C. "Celtic F.C."),
[Wigan Athletic](/wiki/Wigan_Athletic_F.C. "Wigan Athletic F.C.") and
[Sunderland](/wiki/Sunderland_A.F.C. "Sunderland A.F.C."), Belmadi joined
[Southampton](/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C.") (then playing in the
Football League Championship) for their pre-season tour of Scotland. [Harry
Redknapp](/wiki/Harry_Redknapp "Harry Redknapp") initially gave Belmadi a one-
month contract, and he made his debut on 6 August 2005 in a 0–0 draw against
[Wolverhampton Wanderers](/wiki/Wolverhampton_Wanderers "Wolverhampton
Wanderers"). His contract was extended until the end of the 2005–06 season
after impressive performances in his early games, including a goal against
[Crewe Alexandra](/wiki/Crewe_Alexandra_F.C. "Crewe Alexandra F.C.") on 27
August 2005. In January 2006, he picked up a thigh injury, which put him out
of the team until April.

Belmadi had, however, done enough to persuade Southampton, now managed by
[George Burley](/wiki/George_Burley "George Burley"), to re-sign him for the
2006–07 season. This was again blighted by injury problems, including a knee
injury picked up in September, which put him out until February. He picked up
several other niggling injuries putting him out for long periods. When fit,
there was no doubting Belmadi's ability and quality on the ball whether
playing on the left or right of midfield. At his best, he could unpick
defenses with his passing and kept the ball well. Unfortunately, his injuries
restricted him to 40 appearances in his two years at [St
Mary's](/wiki/St_Mary%27s_Stadium "St Mary's Stadium"). His contract with the
Saints expired on 30 June 2007 and was not renewed as Southampton faced up to
the financial realities of a third season in [the
Championship](/wiki/Football_League_Championship "Football League
Championship").[2]

### Valenciennes

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Djamel_Belmadi&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section:
Valenciennes")]

After being released by Southampton, Belmadi returned to France and joined
[Valenciennes](/wiki/Valenciennes_FC "Valenciennes FC"). He retired from
football in 2009.

## International career

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Djamel_Belmadi&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section:
International career")]

Belmadi made his debut for [Algeria](/wiki/Algeria_national_football_team
"Algeria national football team") on 9 July 2000 against
[Morocco](/wiki/Morocco_national_football_team "Morocco national football
team"). He was part of the Algerian [2004 African Nations
Cup](/wiki/2004_African_Nations_Cup "2004 African Nations Cup") team, who
finished second in their group in the first round of competition before being
defeated by Morocco in the quarter-finals. Belmadi last played for Algeria in
a World Cup qualifier against [Zimbabwe](/wiki/Zimbabwe_national_football_team
"Zimbabwe national football team") on 20 June 2004, having made 20 appearances
and scoring 5 goals.

## Managerial career

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Djamel_Belmadi&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section:
Managerial career")]

### Lekhwiya

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Djamel_Belmadi&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section:
Lekhwiya")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/20/Djamel_Belmadi_2011.jpg/250px-
Djamel_Belmadi_2011.jpg)](/wiki/File:Djamel_Belmadi_2011.jpg)Belmadi coaching
Lekhwiya in a [Qatar Stars League](/wiki/Qatar_Stars_League "Qatar Stars
League") match against [Al Sadd](/wiki/Al-Sadd_SC "Al-Sadd SC")

In the summer of 2010, Belmadi was appointed as the head coach of newly
promoted [Qatar Stars League](/wiki/Qatar_Stars_League "Qatar Stars League")
club [Lekhwiya](/wiki/Lekhwiya_SC "Lekhwiya SC").[3] In his first season with
the club, he led them to the [2010–11 Qatar Stars
League](/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Qatar_Stars_League "2010–11 Qatar Stars League")
title for the first time in the club's history. He also led them to the final
of the [2010 Sheikh Jassem Cup](/wiki/2010_Sheikh_Jassem_Cup "2010 Sheikh
Jassem Cup"), where they lost to [Al Arabi](/wiki/Al-Arabi_SC_\(Qatar\) "Al-
Arabi SC \(Qatar\)"). For the second time, [Lekhwiya](/wiki/Lekhwiya_SC
"Lekhwiya SC") won the [2011–12 Qatar Stars
League](/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Qatar_Stars_League "2011–12 Qatar Stars League")
title, under the management of Belmadi. He resigned on 8 October 2012 after a
bad start of the 2012–13 season.

### Qatar B

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Djamel_Belmadi&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section:
Qatar B")]

In December 2013, Belmadi was appointed as head coach of the [Qatar
B](/wiki/Qatar_national_football_team "Qatar national football team") team,
which was set to participate in the [2014 WAFF
Championship](/wiki/2014_WAFF_Championship "2014 WAFF Championship") on home
soil. He called up a number of foreigners to the national team, including
compatriots [Boualem Khoukhi](/wiki/Boualem_Khoukhi "Boualem Khoukhi") and
[Karim Boudiaf](/wiki/Karim_Boudiaf "Karim Boudiaf") after being informed by
the [QFA](/wiki/Qatar_Football_Association "Qatar Football Association") that
they were eligible to compete for Qatar.[4] Qatar were crowned champions of
the 2014 WAFF Championship after defeating
[Jordan](/wiki/Jordan_national_football_team "Jordan national football team")
on 7 January.[5] They finished the tournament undefeated, with 10 goals scored
and a single goal conceded.

### Qatar senior team

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Djamel_Belmadi&action=edit&section=10 "Edit
section: Qatar senior team")]

On 15 March 2014, Belmadi was unveiled as the new head coach of the [Qatar
senior football team](/wiki/Qatar_national_football_team "Qatar national
football team"), replacing [Fahad Thani](/wiki/Fahad_Thani "Fahad Thani").[6]
His first match as Qatar coach was a 0–0 draw with
[Macedonia](/wiki/Macedonia_national_football_team "Macedonia national
football team"). He led his team to a notable 1–0 first-ever victory over
[Australia](/wiki/Australia_men%27s_national_soccer_team "Australia men's
national soccer team") in a friendly match on 14 October 2014, after having
posted a 5–0 win over [Lebanon](/wiki/Lebanon_national_football_team "Lebanon
national football team") and a 3–0 victory over
[Uzbekistan](/wiki/Uzbekistan_national_football_team "Uzbekistan national
football team") in their two previous matches.[7] In correspondence to Qatar's
performance in the aforementioned friendly matches, sports channel [Al
Kass](/wiki/Al-Kass_Sports_Channel "Al-Kass Sports Channel") stated that Qatar
is "showing signs of evolution with Belmadi" and that the team was "undergoing
a renewal."[8] He led Qatar to win the [22nd Arabian Gulf
Cup](/wiki/22nd_Arabian_Gulf_Cup "22nd Arabian Gulf Cup") by beating host
[Saudi Arabia](/wiki/Saudi_Arabia_national_football_team "Saudi Arabia
national football team") in the final. However, Qatar showed a poor form in
the [2015 AFC Asian Cup](/wiki/2015_AFC_Asian_Cup "2015 AFC Asian Cup") and
was eliminated in the group stages after three consecutive defeats by [United
Arab Emirates](/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates_national_football_team "United Arab
Emirates national football team"), [Iran](/wiki/Iran_national_football_team
"Iran national football team") and
[Bahrain](/wiki/Bahrain_national_football_team "Bahrain national football
team"). He was dismissed from his post on 30 April 2015.[9]

### Al-Duhail

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Djamel_Belmadi&action=edit&section=11 "Edit
section: Al-Duhail")]

On 19 June 2015, Belmadi was appointed for the second time in his career to
coach [Lekhwiya](/wiki/Lekhwiya_SC "Lekhwiya SC"); he was a replacement for
[Michael Laudrup](/wiki/Michael_Laudrup "Michael Laudrup"). In 2017, the club
was rebranded to Al-Duhail SC following the absorption of [El
Jaish](/wiki/El_Jaish_SC "El Jaish SC").[_[citation
needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Algeria

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Djamel_Belmadi&action=edit&section=12 "Edit
section: Algeria")]

On 2 August 2018, Belmadi became the manager of the [Algeria national
team](/wiki/Algeria_national_football_team "Algeria national football
team").[10] At his second international football championship (having coached
Qatar in the [2015 AFC Asian Cup](/wiki/2015_AFC_Asian_Cup "2015 AFC Asian
Cup")), Belmadi's Algerian team was not considered a serious contender for the
trophy because Algeria's performance in the [2019 Africa Cup of Nations
qualification](/wiki/2019_Africa_Cup_of_Nations_qualification "2019 Africa Cup
of Nations qualification") was not promising, despite topping the group with
two draws to [Gambia](/wiki/Gambia_national_football_team "Gambia national
football team") and an away-loss to [Benin](/wiki/Benin_national_football_team
"Benin national football team"). The unimpressive qualification campaign
increased the pressure on Belmadi.

Despite heavy criticism, Belmadi led Algeria to success and earned his first
international trophy. Algeria defeated every opponent on its road to the final
of the [2019 Africa Cup of Nations](/wiki/2019_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2019
Africa Cup of Nations") (AFCON) held in Egypt, including two victories over
[Senegal](/wiki/Senegal_national_football_team "Senegal national football
team") in the group stage and the
[final](/wiki/2019_Africa_Cup_of_Nations_Final "2019 Africa Cup of Nations
Final"). Algeria won its second continental title and became the North African
second team, after [Egypt](/wiki/Egypt_national_football_team "Egypt national
football team"), to win more than one AFCON trophy.[11]

In the [2021 AFCON](/wiki/2021_Africa_Cup_of_Nations "2021 Africa Cup of
Nations"), the defending champions Algeria finished last in their group to be
eliminated from the tournament.[12] During the [2022 World Cup
qualification](/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_\(CAF\) "2022 FIFA
World Cup qualification \(CAF\)") third round, Algeria failed to qualify to
the final tournament in Qatar, having lost on away goals rule against
[Cameroon](/wiki/Cameroon_national_football_team "Cameroon national football
team") following a 2–2 draw on aggregate.[13]

In January 2023, Belmadi extended his contract until 2026.[14]

In the [2023 AFCON](/wiki/2023_Africa_Cup_of_Nations_Group_D "2023 Africa Cup
of Nations Group D") held in [Ivory Coast](/wiki/Ivory_Coast "Ivory Coast"),
Algeria led by Belmadi exited the tournament after their defeat against
[Mauritania](/wiki/Mauritania_national_football_team "Mauritania national
football team"), without scoring any win in the group phase.[15] On 24 January
2024, Belmadi's position as national team manager was terminated by mutual
consent.[16] However, despite immediately resigning himself in front of the
players, Belmadi asked the [FAF](/wiki/Algerian_Football_Federation "Algerian
Football Federation") for a severance package worth 29 months of salary,
equivalent to €7 million. Faced with a refusal from the FAF, he then
threatened to bring the matter to the FIFA for a ruling.[17]

### Return to Al-Duhail

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Djamel_Belmadi&action=edit&section=13 "Edit
section: Return to Al-Duhail")]

In June 2025, Belmadi returned to Al-Duhail for his third spell as head
coach.[18]

## Bank theft incident

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Djamel_Belmadi&action=edit&section=14 "Edit
section: Bank theft incident")]

While Belmadi was with Manchester City, he, along with players [Daniel Van
Buyten](/wiki/Daniel_Van_Buyten "Daniel Van Buyten") and [Vicente
Vuoso](/wiki/Vicente_Mat%C3%ADas_Vuoso "Vicente Matías Vuoso"), were the
victims of a theft by two bank workers. At the time that Belmadi left
Manchester City, he left £230,000 in an account with the [Co-operative
Bank](/wiki/The_Co-operative_Bank "The Co-operative Bank"). In total, the bank
workers stole more than £350,000 from the accounts of the three players.
